reviews.evidence: Ships an adaptive reasoning-effort slider, snap/commit behavior, model/subagent visibility rules, a visual skin/native toggle, one screenshot, install verification, uninstall, and concrete troubleshooting notes.
reviews.concern: The README states features rather than an explicit user scenario, and operational use beyond toggling the skin and moving the slider is limited.

reviews.evidence: Provides a broad desktop assistant layer with multiple runtimes, global launcher and reply, scheduling, screen and meeting context, dictation, memory, worktrees, review board, remote access, and confirmed-action computer control, demonstrated across many screenshots and GIFs.
reviews.concern: It is explicitly an early Apple-Silicon macOS release, and the README offers little troubleshooting or recovery guidance for its many advanced workflows.

reviews.evidence: Delivers a Windows minimal preset that discovers Git Bash, executes commands through it, enforces sandbox policy, and handles timeouts, background work, truncation, and diagnostics; usage, limits, configuration bounds, and ten unit-test cases are stated.
reviews.concern: The shipped scope is narrow, each call starts a fresh shell, restricted Windows sandboxes cannot run it, and no concrete successful command output is shown.

reviews.evidence: Offers phone-adapted remote DSH access through a Quick Tunnel with one-time pairing, optional GitHub identity, per-device sessions, revocation, HTTP/WebSocket authentication, network fallback, and update prompting; the README gives a scan-to-connect path and several scenario narratives.
reviews.concern: Most operational, compatibility, threat-model, and troubleshooting detail is deferred to linked documents, while the visible demonstration evidence is largely static promotional material.

reviews.evidence: Covers an end-to-end invoice workflow: IMAP collection, filtering, archive extraction, PDF-link recovery, OCR/vision/local fallback, field extraction, matching, classification, manual-review routing, and Excel reporting, with OS-specific starts, diagrams, an output tree, troubleshooting, privacy, and failure boundaries.
reviews.concern: The use-case coverage remains concentrated on one reimbursement scenario, no actual report contents are shown, and the README states no explicit automated test evidence.

reviews.evidence: Coordinates a local content lifecycle from topic and script files through Screen Studio binding, subtitles, covers, publishing drafts, and metric sync, while preserving ordinary files and explicit human approval boundaries; it includes setup and first-content prompts, artifact layout, graceful optional dependencies, tests, release checks, and migration guidance.
reviews.concern: Only one worked content example is provided, representative artifact contents or completed publication outcomes are not shown, and detailed tool operations are delegated to linked documentation.

reviews.evidence: Implements reusable multi-model teams with member policies, bounded DAG planning, activation modes, background execution, retries, quality repair, durable run inspection, token attribution, versions, recipes, backup/import, and exports; five-step use, advanced settings, screenshots, failure semantics, rollback, security limits, compatibility, and extensive validation are documented.
reviews.concern: Despite exhaustive reference material, explicit applied task scenarios are sparse and no representative final team synthesis or end-to-end case outcome is shown.

reviews.evidence: Combines execution/plan state, standard/first-principles reasoning, two independent quality gates, and human-approved cross-session learning rules; it supplies scenario-specific mode combinations, command reference, review formats, proposal management, backup recovery, strict learning bounds, compatibility validation, migration, and failure retention.
reviews.concern: There is no worked end-to-end task showing the resulting answer and review outcome, and the current release supports one exact Harness version.

reviews.evidence: States an end-to-end multi-model A-share workflow spanning market data, stock selection, live execution, monitoring, strategy adjustment, risk controls, DingTalk chat, natural-language orders, batch/conditional trades, cancellation, and remote app launch, with concrete command syntax and examples.
reviews.concern: Results are only linked externally, automated test evidence is absent, many broad trading claims lack visible validation, and the complete usable product depends on a separately licensed closed-source executable.

reviews.evidence: Provides multi-provider balance and quota monitoring, token and cost analytics, budgets, refresh scheduling, many built-in and declarative adapters, drill-down views, secret-free CSV/JSON exports, and loopback APIs; it includes comprehensive configuration and recovery paths plus detailed security, correctness, compatibility, offline-test, and live-validation evidence.
reviews.concern: Explicit user scenarios are limited relative to the reference depth, and only one interface preview is shown without representative CSV, JSON, budget-alert, or failure-state output.
